text:
maya: quick heads-up — the canary for rtv-v3 is spiking 5xx and tail latency. seeing KV miss rate jump on prefix-cache for session/.
andrew: saw that too. errors start ~12:05 UTC. console shows traffic split 10% canary
sarah: @maya can you pause canary? prefer quick-pause then investigate KV TTL + quorum
maya: request: Fast pause then run stale-kv scan. If pause fails, fallback to split->0%.
deploy-bot: build 2026.03.18-rc5 deployed to canary at 12:01 UTC
kevin: steps I suggest:
1) `redwood rollout pause --id canary-rtv-v3` (fast stop routing)
2) `rwctl kv scan --prefix session/ --since 24h --flag=stale` to find stale shard keys
3) if stale > 0.5% run `rwctl kv invalidate --keys-file stale.txt --drain=true`
4) reduce quota for canary: `redwood quota update --route /chat --limit 0.01` for canary tag
sarah: + check metrics: canary error-rate, tail P99 latency, KV hit-rate, cache-size. Dashboards: /dash/rtv/canary
maya: I'm going to run the pause now
maya: `redwood rollout pause --id canary-rtv-v3`
deploy-bot: Rollout canary-rtv-v3 pause initiated by maya at 12:14 UTC — state: PAUSING
ops-oncall: monitor logs for 429/503 thundering herd. If we see backlog spike, we need to scale fallback pool
andrew: After pause completes, run a health probe `curl -H "x-canary:1" https://api.redwood.internal/rtv/health` to assert no residual routing
maya: pause completed. traffic dropped to 0% canary. KV miss rate still elevated but trending down after cache TTL eviction
kevin: recs for post-mortem: add a pre-pause check in console: a single-click 'pause & run KV-sanity' that bundles the commands. Also automations to reduce canary quota before full pause
sarah: agree — UX guard: warn if KV miss > 0.2% and suggest `stale-scan` before pause
maya: filing a ticket in ops board with steps + logs -> https://redwood.ops/tickets/RTV-342
andrew: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. will follow up with root cause analysis once stale-keys list lands
